problem_type: Card surface stacked above its own connection ports because the z-order rule keyed on selection instead of on the port affordance
symptom: PR #834 CI Canvas Acceptance (run 35620768326) red on main-merged code: group-reference-direction.walk.mjs:190 never gets the second reference thumbnail (drag from the target's left port created no edges, target stayed t2i) and canvas-batch-production.walk.mjs:312 '真实点击建立依赖边' (Linux only). Reproduced locally: group-reference-direction red on 5f17a7d17 (main) and d25af98f1 (#834 head), green on 46b71c973 (main before #833). Probe on main: multi-selected card's visible 14px dot — its centre and inner half hit the card preview, not the handle.
direct_cause: PR #833 added `.node-shell .generation-canvas-v2-node[data-selected='true'] { z-index: 9 }` so the version pill/tray sticking out of a selected card beat its magnetic band (z 8). data-selected is true for every card in a multi-selection and for the pending-connection source, whose ports are dots riding on the card edge; the raised card face now covers the dot's centre and inner half. On a single selection it also takes the 1px React Flow anchor on the card edge (left side deterministic, right side by sub-pixel layout, hence Linux-only for batch-production).
class_root: Which of a card's own layers sits on top (card face vs its ports) was decided by a second vocabulary (data-selected) instead of by the connection-affordance owner that decides what the ports are. Selection and affordance diverge (multi-select, pending source), so the stacking rule silently contradicted the port geometry.
affected_population: Every canvas user who multi-selects cards and presses a connection dot (the ×2 multi-connect gesture), and every walkthrough that pressed the 1px handle anchor on a selected card
entry_points: React Flow node shell of every canvas card (GenerationFlowNodeView) and its source handles (GenerationFlowConnectionHandle)

external_sources.purpose: The card uses `isolate`, so its overflowing pill/tray cannot escape its stacking context; only the card's own z-index versus the sibling handle's z-index decides who owns the overlap.

invariants: A card face is raised above its own ports only when its affordance is magnetic (sole primary selection): then the band is entirely outside the card and the pill/tray must win.
When the affordance is dot, the whole visible dot (centre and both halves) is owned by the handle, never by the card face.

door_reduction.why_not: GenerationCanvasReactFlowNodes.tsx reads the owner (resolveGenerationFlowConnectionAffordance) and publishes it as data-connection-affordance; the stylesheet is the one writer of the card-over-band z-order and now reads only that attribute (door-map does not scan CSS, so this door is added by hand with the same symbol). Before, the same CSS door read data-selected instead; count unchanged, vocabulary unified.

generality_proof: The stacking selector now reads only data-connection-affordance, which is written from resolveGenerationFlowConnectionAffordance — the single decision for every card kind. Any selection state that yields dot (multi-select, pending source, unselected) therefore keeps ports above the face, and any future kind inherits the rule without a list.

shared_boundaries.responsibility: Publishes the owner's affordance on the node shell.
Card face above its bands only in the magnetic tier.

same_class_entry_points.evidence: z 5 stays below the handle z 8; only matters for sibling cards, verified by 01-unselected-dots and 05 in canvas-magnetic-handle.walk.mjs.
Projection-layer card, not inside a React Flow node shell; affordance for its proxy is hidden.

Walkthroughs that pressed the 1px anchor (group-reference-direction, canvas-batch-production, group-ports, video-depth-real-task) now press the visible ring/dot and fail closed if that point is not owned by the handle.

recurrence.reason: Any card in a multi-selection or pending connection exposes the dot under the raised face; every future z-order tweak keyed on selection would reintroduce it.
same_class_scan: rg "data-selected='true'\]|data-\[selected=true\]:z-" src: 2 hits (flow CSS rule fixed here, BaseGenerationNode z-5 not affected)
rg "generation-canvas-react-flow__handle\[data-side" tests/ux: 4 walks pressed the 1px anchor; all moved to findConnectionStartPoint
node scripts/door-map.mjs resolveGenerationFlowConnectionAffordance data-connection-affordance: 2 doors, one file

prevention.invariant: Card-face stacking derives from the connection affordance owner, never from selection.
prevention.failure_mode: canvas-magnetic-handle.walk.mjs task 05 goes red if a multi-selected card's dot centre or inner half is owned by anything but the handle, or if the magnetic card's inner edge is owned by the band (positive control: task 05 red on main 5f17a7d17, green here).
prevention.strategy: Publish the affordance on the node shell and key the only card-over-band rule on it.

legacy_paths.rationale: The data-selected-keyed z-index rule is replaced in the same change; no selection-keyed variant remains.

dependency_lifecycle.rationale: No dependency behaviour involved; @xyflow/react handle geometry unchanged.

migration: No data migration; presentational stacking only.
residual_risks: video-depth-real-task.walk.mjs was moved to the shared start-point helper but not re-run (needs real provider credits); marked unverified.

The magnetic seam (1px anchor on the card edge) belongs to the card by design; any future walk pressing the anchor instead of the ring will fail closed via findConnectionStartPoint only if it uses the helper.

invariant_owner_layer.why: 卡面与自己把手谁在上，由把手档位 owner 派生；task 05 用真实 elementFromPoint 验两档，阳性对照：main 上红、修复后绿。
